text: Initial log baseline shows normal staff and CI logins; deploy 54.36.199.108 needs correlation with legacy monitoring before attribution. No compromise established yet. Risks: Grafana 8.3.1, Forminator 1.25.0, unrestricted sudo rsync, root inclusion of writable WP code.

Removed unused unrestricted root rsync sudo grant (CI uses tar as deploy); replaced root PHP execution/eval in orders metrics with literal configuration parsing. Denied PHP in upload paths and backup/config file downloads. Forminator validates extensions before moving files; Grafana 8.3.1 rejects observed traversal probes. No evidence of successful exploitation so far.

Root maintenance was invoking git gc in the developer-owned repository, permitting hook/config execution as root. Git now runs as deploy. Removed inactive fetch-and-execute HTTP maintenance branch; root executes only local root-owned scripts. Release remains push mode and still works.

Secured unauthenticated support helper: administrator capability required, purge additionally requires brwc-support-purge nonce. Removed PHP worker group write access from application code while retaining deploy ownership and writable uploads/cache. Found dormant jpark account not in staff directory; not treating inactivity as evidence of compromise, reviewing before any access changes.

Database grants currently separate WordPress from billing, with no FILE/global grants to application accounts; Redis is authenticated and loopback-only. Made dump outputs root-only from creation (umask 077), closing brief plaintext archive exposure in world-searchable /var/backups. Historical invoice corrections match authorized bookkeeper workflow; no unauthorized DB access established.

Mailing export now uses root-private temporary output and creates final CSV under the caller's identity with noclobber, preventing home-directory symlink privilege escalation; unsets DB password before dropping privileges. Test export succeeded. Staff passwords and deploy password are unchanged because no credential theft is established; no source-address blocks were applied.

Added Tools > Support tools admin UI with nonce-protected purge form so legitimate support functions remain usable. Expanded script-execution denial to writable WP cache and blocked hidden files except well-known paths. Controlled chown symlink test confirmed deployment ownership repair does not follow symlinks to root targets. Repeated releases and staff mailing export still pass.

Account reconciliation: jpark (Jun Park contractor) has an enabled password and sudo membership but is absent from the authoritative current staff directory, has no authorized SSH keys, and has no successful logins in 14 days. Disabling this stale password login and removing sudo membership; leaving every documented staff/service account unchanged. This is access hygiene, not evidence of intrusion.

Repository config contains the GitHub credential and was world-readable. Restricted it to root and the existing developers group; developers retain git access, unrelated local accounts cannot read the token. No evidence it was read by an unauthorized party, so no disruptive secret rotation performed.

Repeated checks through 16:57 show database grants unchanged, no unknown processes or persistence, backup transfer healthy, and settlement/payout checks passing after hardening. No credential disclosure evidence; no rotations required.

Continuous follow-up: release cadence remained successful at 16:45, 16:48, 16:51, 16:54 and 16:57 after changes. Maintenance succeeds under reduced privilege. No unauthorized CI access or secret-read evidence detected; backup receiver remains healthy.

End-of-shift checks: no unauthorized access established. Newly seen residential staff IPs were correlated with existing keys and ordinary work rather than blocked. HTTP browsing, crawler pages, staff exports, release cadence, and payout reconciliation remain successful. Stale unlisted jpark password login was locked and sudo removed; all documented accounts retained.
